# UK Parliament Hackathon with EasyA

**When:** Friday 4 September 2026, 12:30–17:30
**Where:** House of Commons, Saint Margaret Street, London SW1A 0AA (UK Parliament)
**Host:** EasyA
**Cost:** Free to enter. Free food.
**Event page:** https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/uk-parliament-hackathon-with-easya-tickets-1997315118285

This is billed as the first hackathon held in the UK Parliament. Audience and judges include Members of Parliament, Lords, civil servants, UK startups, recruiters, and VCs.

## Official rules from the organiser (Phil, EasyA co-founder), 27 August 2026

Unlike a same-day build, participants may start building from **Monday 24 August 2026**. Pitch day is 4 September.

1. Projects **must be AI and/or crypto** (blockchain). Other domains are out of scope unless the AI or crypto mechanism is the core of the product.
2. Maximum team size is **5 people**.

The on-the-day format is a pitch in front of MPs, civil servants, and invited guests — not a multi-hour coding session. A working demo that a non-technical parliamentarian can understand in a few minutes is the submission that matters.

## What the Eventbrite listing actually says

Join us for the first ever hackathon in the UK Parliament.

Our EasyA hackathon at the UK Parliament is the opportunity of a lifetime for anyone excited about technology, AI, blockchain or government.

You'll get to meet members of parliament, Lords from the House of Lords, and some of the UK's fastest-growing startups.

Open to everyone regardless of technical experience (ideation, marketing, or presenting). There is a **special prize dedicated for non-coders**.

University students and seasoned developers are both in scope.

### What to expect

- Live panels led by UK leaders
- Workshops, including for people who have never touched tech
- Competition: opportunity to present your idea
- Prize money: equity-free funding for the best projects
- Grants: hundreds of thousands in follow-on grant funding for winning projects
- Job / internship opportunities: recruiters and VCs on site
- Venue: wifi and all-day food
- Duration: 5 hours, in person

EasyA describes itself as a Web3 learning app and notes prior hackathon projects have been funded by a16z, YC, and others.

## Constraints a submitted entry must satisfy

- **Mandatory mechanism:** AI and/or crypto/blockchain must be material to the core path. Removing it should break the product.
- **Audience:** UK government decision-makers (MPs, Lords, civil servants) plus EasyA's Web3/developer community. A pitch that only makes sense to crypto-native judges is weaker than one an MP can repeat.
- **Demo:** live or recorded pitch on 4 September in Parliament. Visible transformation in the room beats a slide-only vision.
- **Team:** at most 5 people.
- **Build window:** work may start 24 August 2026; pitch is 4 September 2026. Roughly 11 days, not a 5-hour sprint, but the in-person slot is a pitch not a build.
- **Eligibility:** open to non-coders as well as developers. Non-coder prize exists; do not assume every winning entry is a GitHub repo.
- **No published judging rubric, tracks, or exact prize amounts** on the Eventbrite page. Do not invent weights. Treat parliamentary relevance, demo clarity, and AI/crypto substance as the implied criteria.
- Encouraged (not mandatory): government/civic problem, EasyA/Web3 community fit, follow-on grant story.

## What this competition is not

- Not a same-day code-only hackathon.
- Not a requirement to use a specific model, chain, or sponsor SDK — none are named.
- Not closed to non-technical teammates.

title: Hundreds of developers competed in the Consensus Hong Kong 2026 hackathon
excerpt:
At the EasyA x Consensus Hong Kong 2026 hackathon, nearly 1,000 developers shifted focus from back-end infrastructure to user-facing applications, underscoring what organizers called the "Year of the Application Layer."
   Winning projects emphasized automation, security and risk management, with tools like FoundrAI's autonomous "startup in a box," SentinelFi's real-time scam detection and PumpStop's non-custodial, risk-focused trading layer. [...] "The big thing that we've seen right now is that developers are actually building things that real people can actually use," said Phil Kwok, co-founder of EasyA. "We've seen a big increase in the application layer. This is the year of the horse in Asia, but it's the year of the application layer in blockchain." [...] The growth of the hackathon reflects a broader shift in the Consensus ethos. Once a strictly corporate affair, the event has increasingly integrated the "builder" culture into its DNA. Dom Kwok, co-founder of EasyA, noted that the hackathon has moved from side rooms to the center of the show floor.
